subject: Data lifespan alignment & forensic snapshot request — Crescent Health
messages:
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@crescenthealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Gaurav Patel <gpatel@crescenthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on segmented retention windows & forensics snapshot

Diego —

Thanks for the demo last week. We have a follow-up for the security team: Crescent Health operates on a "segmented retention" model where different data slices (PII, diagnostic logs, ephemeral interaction traces) have different lifespans. Your SOC2 scope and the SIG answers list a default 90-day log TTL, but our legal team requires a 180-day forensic snapshot for any incident that impacts patient-matching flows.

Can Redwood provide:
- A clear mapping of which Redwood log classes are covered by the 90d default vs which can be configured to 180d?
- The technical mechanism for creating a forensics snapshot that preserves KV caches and conversation context at request-time (we need chain-of-custody metadata).
- Evidence we can include in our SIG/CAIQ response showing retention controls and an example snapshot manifest.

We may need a limited, customer-specific exception that applies only to our tenant and only for legal-hold windows. Please advise next steps and whether you need any formal legal request or POA.

Sofia Martinez
Director, Security & Privacy
Crescent Health

--

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Gaurav Patel <gpatel@crescenthealth.com>, mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on segmented retention windows & forensics snapshot

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers up-front, then I’ll loop in engineering for the manifest and playbook.

- Redwood default retention: application traces and unstructured request logs are on the 90d default. Interaction-level ephemeral traces (KV caches, short-term request context) are purged after 30d unless a customer opts into "extended forensics".
- Customer-specific exceptions: we support tenant-scoped retention overrides for a subset of data classes (audit logs, request/response archives, and diagnostic slices). That override is enforcement-scoped (only the tenant) and recorded in the config audit trail.
- Forensics snapshot: we can produce a timebound snapshot that includes request/response archives, KV cache dumps, and a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and our internal chain-of-custody fields (who requested, request_id, server image id).

Action items I propose:
1) I'll prepare an engineering playbook and a sample manifest (will attach) — needs review by your legal/security.
2) Mina (copied) will propose the minimal retention mapping matrix so you can show it on the SIG.
3) If Crescent wants the 180d retention for the forensic window, we'll need a signed addendum describing scope and legal-hold triggers (we can template this).

Attaching a short matrix and a draft playbook — consider them starting points. If you want an offline call, we can do a 30-min technical walk-through with engineering.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: segmented_retention_matrix.csv, forensics_playbook_v1.pdf

--

From: mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@crescenthealth.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on segmented retention windows & forensics snapshot

Sofia —

Attached is the retention matrix in CSV and a condensed playbook PDF (same package Diego referenced). Key points for inclusion in SIG/CAIQ responses:
- Data classes we can override for a tenant: audit_logs, request_response_archive, diagnostic_slices.
- Data classes we cannot extend without code change: ephemeral_kv_cache (we persist cache dumps only at snapshot time).
- Chain-of-custody fields included in snapshot manifest: requested_by, request_id, timestamp_utc, operator_hash, server_build_id, manifest_signature.

Example entry from the CSV (for SIG language):
"audit_logs, tenant-scoped, override=180d, retention-enforced, evidence=exportable, chain_of_custody=present"

If Crescent needs immutable long-term storage beyond 365d we recommend export to customer-controlled S3 (we can automate exports to an S3 bucket or GCP storage with lifecycle rules).

Laura — can you confirm if the compliance addendum template (limited-scope retention) is the same as the one we used for Meridian last quarter or if legal updated the clause?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Product Security Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: crescent_evidence_manifest.txt

--

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@crescenthealth.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on segmented retention windows & forensics snapshot

Sofia / Gaurav —

Following up: legal reviewed the limited-scope retention addendum and confirmed we can support a tenant-specific 180-day forensic retention for the requested data classes. High-level notes:

- Scope: applies only to audit_logs, request_response_archive, diagnostic_slices. Does NOT apply to ephemeral_kv_cache except as included in timebound snapshots.
- Triggers: a legal-hold request from Crescent legal or a signed incident declaration is required to start the hold. Our ops team will mark the tenant and lock retention policy for the window specified.
- Evidence & attestation: we will provide a signed snapshot manifest plus a CSV summary (attached) showing the object ids, checksums, and retention timestamps. You can surface these artifacts in SIG/CAIQ as "customer-specific forensics evidence".

Next step: if you confirm, Diego will send the addendum template and a prefilled example with Crescent details so your legal can sign. Rishi, please queue the work item to enable tenant-scoped overrides and the automated snapshot workflow (internal ticket HS-0004921).

Happy to join a call with Crescent legal if helpful.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Security & Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: crescent_evidence_manifest.txt
